Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking demos today. Quick recap and the plan I promised: 

Summary from today
- Primary goals: low-latency customer-facing QA (95th pct < 220ms target), and throughput for bulk indexing (~1M docs/week).
- Quality bar: F1-style precision on entity extraction + fewer hallucinations on short prompts.
- Constraint: infra cost target ~25% below current vendor budget.

What we recommend next (shortlist + rationale)
1) Redwood-1.7q (quantized 7B) — baseline pick for latency/cost. Good token-efficiency and strong extraction quality in our head-to-head.
2) OpenLong-13 (int8) — higher quality for edge cases (longer context), cost ~2x of Redwood-1.7q but better at complex reasoning.
3) Guard-3.5 (safety-tuned mid) — backup for hallucination-sensitive flows; slightly faster than OpenLong on short prompts.

Deliverables I attached to this thread:
- finrise_prompt_pack_v1.md (sample prompts & paired evals)
- finrise_benchmarks_summary.csv (latency/cost/quality snapshots across typical prompt sets)
- redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf (ballpark committed vs. pay-as-you-go)

Next steps (action items)
- Alex: pick 1 primary and 1 fallback engine for a 2-week eval (by EOD Wed).
- We (Redwood): deploy a sandbox project with sample prompt pack + benchmark harness and share Drive link (ETA: 48 hours).
- Marissa: loop in Solutions Eng to produce a short-runbook for caching & KV settings for QA use-case.

If you want, we can also start a canary rollout plan with automatic fallback rules so you never miss the SLA during the trial.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks. Attaching the quick prompt guidance you asked for and the benchmark slices we ran against your sample dataset. Highlights below, and full artifacts are in the Drive link.

Key prompt fixes for entity extraction (apply in order)
- Prefer explicit instruction framing: e.g., "Return JSON with keys: entity, type, start, end. If unsure, return "unknown" rather than guessing."
- Use 2-shot positive examples for the tricky types (we included 3 in finrise_prompt_pack_v1.md).
- Add a short canonicalizer post-process (lowercasing + punctuation strip) before scoring to reduce false mismatches.

Benchmark highlights (from finrise_benchmarks_summary.csv)
- Redwood-1.7q: median latency 68ms, p95 185ms, precision 0.88 on extraction set, cost unit 1x.
- OpenLong-13: median latency 210ms, p95 365ms, precision 0.93, cost ~2.1x.
- Guard-3.5: median latency 95ms, p95 240ms, precision 0.90, cost ~1.4x.

Operational note on regression risk
- If you deploy Redwood-1.7q with aggressive caching, watch for stale prefix issues on prompts with dynamic context — we recommend TTL=30s for session-level keys during evaluation.
- We’ll run a simple regression harness against your golden set daily and surface any >2% drop in precision.
